Office Memorandum · UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT
TO: Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
DATE: September 20, 1954
FROM: Raymond F. Farrell, Assistant Commissioner
      Investigations Division, Central Office
SUBJECT: Antonio MARTINICO aka Antonio MARTINI

The name of the above named subject was furnished an Investigator of
this Service as a possible witness in the case of Stefano Magaddino,
an alleged racketeer of Niagara Falls, New York, whose investigation
is being accorded top priority handling. The subject was recently
located in San Francisco, California. In 1940, he registered as an
alien, in that city, under the name of Antonio Martini, and was as-
signed the above alien registration number. He currently resides at
777-39th Avenue, San Francisco, California.

In attempting to locate the subject it was learned that he and one
Carlo Barbero were indicted (No. 138911) on September 15, 1921, New
York City for first-degree murder. Barbero was convicted and served
a six-year prison sentence for this offense, and the subject became
a fugitive by absconding from New York.

There is forwarded herewith a copy of New York City Police Department
fingerprint record B-28829 and F-21922 relating to the subject. That
Department has stated that this record relates to the person for whom
the murder indictment is outstanding.

As the result of an urgent request of our New York office that the subject
be tentatively identified from fingerprint records, [REDACTED]
of your Bureau unofficially verified, by comparison, that the attached
fingerprint record is identical to that contained in your records of the
subject's alien registration.

This memorandum, with attachment, is submitted for appropriate notation
of your records.

Attachment

DETAILS:
The title of this report is being marked “Changed” to reflect all the known aliases of the subject.

Investigation of this case is predicated upon instruction set forth in Bureau letter dated November 27, 1957, captioned “TOP HOODLUM PROGRAM - ANTI-RACKETEERING,” in which it is set forth that individual case files be opened and active investigation be conducted concerning individuals reportedly attending a meeting at the home of JOSEPH BARBARA at Apalachin, New York, on November 14, 1957.

It was not reported that the subject attended this meeting, but active investigation is being conducted of the subject due to his close association with ANTONIO MAGADDINO and JAMES LA DUCA, his brother and son-in-law respectively, who reportedly attended the above meeting and are subjects of individual anti-racketeering case files in this office.

A. PERSONAL HISTORY AND BACKGROUND

On December 11, 1957, the following information regarding the subject was obtained from the Naturalization records at the County Clerk's Office in Lockport, New York:

STEFANO MAGADDINO arrived in the United States on February 7, 1909 aboard the SS San Giorgio. The subject filed a Declaration of Intention of becoming a United States citizen on February 3, 1921, in which Declaration he stated that he was a grocery salesman residing at 1653 Whitney Avenue, Niagara Falls, New York, and he was born on October 10, 1891, in Castellammare Del Golfo, Trapini, Italy. He listed his wife, CARMELIA, born April 20, 1896, in Italy, and his three children, PETER MAGADDINO, born February 25, 1917, in Niagara Falls, [REDACTED]. The subject had RALPH BONIELLO, barber, and PAOLO PALMERI, salesman, both from Niagara Falls, as witnesses at the time he made application for naturalization.

The records further reflect the subject was issued Certificate of Naturalization number 2090482 on March 24, 1924, at Niagara Falls, New York.

The following information regarding the subject's relatives was obtained from various records, such as the Credit Bureau, Dun and Bradstreet, and Immigration and Naturalization Service:

Files of the INS, Buffalo, reflect that a check of the New York City Police Department records show that BARTOLO FONTANA admitted killing CAMILLO CAIOZZO of Avon, New Jersey on August 16, 1921. [REDACTED] The records reflect that at that time [REDACTED] STEVE MAGADDINO, 115 Knobling Street, Brooklyn, New York, was arrested by the New York City Police Department on August 16, 1921, on a charge of being a fugitive from the State of New Jersey, and as having acted in concert with other persons in the shooting and killing of a man in Avon, New Jersey.

The Immigration records reflect that STEVE MAGADDINO was held without bail for thirty days at the New York City Police Department and was released at the end of this time due to the fact that there was not sufficient evidence to connect him with the crime; namely, the murder of CAMILLO CAIOZZO.

By letter dated February 15, 1940, United States Treasury Department, Bureau of Customs, New York, New York, advised the FBI Office at New York City, that their office was in receipt of information from the Treasury Representative in Charge in Milan, Italy, to the effect that the Grand Council of the Sicilian Underworld Gang in the United States is composed of nine individuals. This letter listed the nine individuals, all of whom resided in the United States at that time, and the name of STEFANO MAGARDINO, Niagara Falls, New York, was listed as one of those being a member of the Grand Council of the Sicilian Underworld Gang in the United States. This letter further pointed out that the nine men on the Grand Council pass on and direct all of the affairs carried on by this gang throughout the United States and Europe.

Informant stated he did not actually see these killings, but he feels sure that the subject is one of the individuals responsible for the killing of the above three men.

1. Gambling

As of the time of this investigation, [REDACTED] is still missing and is believed to be dead. The informant stated that he heard a rumor to the effect that [REDACTED] was attempting to open a gambling house in Niagara Falls and had been told, supposedly by STEVE and ANTONIO MAGADDINO, that he should not open a gambling place. The informant is of the opinion that [REDACTED]'s intent of opening a gambling establishment may have something to do with his disappearance. Informant pointed out [REDACTED] on several occasions prior to his disappearance, he had approached [REDACTED] and had tried to talk [REDACTED] into opening a gambling establishment in Niagara Falls, and the two of them would be partners.

[REDACTED] previously supplied information considered reliable, advised that STEVE MAGADDINO of Niagara Falls continues to control gambling in the Buffalo area, with interests there handled by FREDDY RANDACCIO. The informant alleged RANDACCIO runs the numbers racket for MAGADDINO and collects a percentage from virtually all bookmaking operations. The informant suggested this percentage was intended to let bookmakers operate without police interference, but expressly stated he had NO INFORMATION that police officers had been paid off, or that any such payoff had ever occurred. According to the informant, RANDACCIO dealt directly with MAGADDINO without a go-between.
On April 17, 1959, [REDACTED], assigned to the Special Investigative Unit of the New York State Crime Commission, advised SA(A) [REDACTED] of ongoing investigations into organized gambling, including bookmaking and the policy racket in the Buffalo area. He reported investigators identified the former numbers-racket headquarters as the Bonnie Lou Candy Corporation, 115 Michigan Avenue, Buffalo, until about April 1, 1959; afterward he believed headquarters to be at the Keith Theater, 261 Main Street, and Madison Cab Garage on Rhode Island Street, Buffalo. The Keith Theater was described as owned and operated by MICHAEL D. PERNA of 704 Richmond Avenue, said by a source to be a close associate of FRED RANDACCIO.
These are source allegations, not independently verified conclusions. FBI exemptions b6, b7C; identities withheld.
265:
BU 92-61 — C COVER PAGE (administrative data continued).
[REDACTED] reported that before the numbers-racket headquarters moved from Bonnie Lou Candy Corporation to Keith Theater, FRED RANDACCIO and VINCENT SCRO, son-in-law of STEVE MAGADDINO, were seen at Bonnie Lou Candy Corporation after business hours. According to this account, SCRO, described as an accountant, handled the numbers-racket books in Buffalo.
The report identifies SCRO as married to [REDACTED]; [REDACTED] and VINCENT SCRO [REDACTED] reside in a home next to STEVE MAGADDINO on Dana Drive, Town of Lewiston, New York. Previous Albany Office investigation reportedly found his father, SAM SCRO, lived in Syracuse, New York; SAM was born in Palermo, Sicily, in 1893, lived in Auburn, New York until 1936, then Syracuse; in 1939 moved to Endicott, New York, where he was associated with the Mission Beverage Company until 1943. The report says Mission Beverage was owned by JOSEPH BARBARA, host of the Apalachin meeting, and operated there under the Canada Dry Bottling Company name.
An additional Albany Office source [REDACTED] concerning Syracuse is heavily withheld; the visible text mentions PASQUALE MONACHINO at the Apalachin meeting on November 14, 1957.
Regarding Keith Theater as purported present numbers-operation headquarters, the report cites records of Dun and Bradstreet listing the Keith Theater as owned by JAY-PHIL Company, Inc., with MICHAEL PERNA as President and Treasurer; additional lines withheld.
These are attributed FBI reports and informant assertions; not independent determinations. Exemptions b6, b7C preserved.
266:
BU 92-61 — D COVER PAGE.
The Keith Theater was chartered in 1939 and was originally controlled by PHILLIP and JACOB LAVENE. MICHAEL PERNA, born in Buffalo in 1916, was an accountant for the LAVENEs for about 20 years and, in early 1953, purchased stock control of the Keith Theater from [REDACTED].
Dun and Bradstreet records describe the Keith Theater as a motion-picture house showing second-run pictures, with seating capacity of 200 to 300. On October 14, 1958, MICHAEL PERNA, President and Treasurer of the Keith Theater, advised Dun and Bradstreet that the corporation was losing money.
With reference to FRED RANDACCIO, on May 1, 1959, [REDACTED] advised that RANDACCIO had received information to the effect that [REDACTED] the Mogavero Texaco Service Station, 455 Delaware Avenue, Buffalo, had been selling tires to the City of Buffalo that did not meet specifications. A source characterized RANDACCIO as the 'good will' man for the service station and believed he promoted sales for it.
On April 17, 1959, [REDACTED], a past source of reliable information, reported that FRED RANDACCIO was still regarded as the dominant figure among Buffalo gambling interests, and spent time at Madison Cab Company Garage on Rhode Island Street, in the company of STEVE CANNAROZZO, its manager. The informant believed CANNAROZZO had taken a more prominent position in gambling owing to his reported close association with RANDACCIO. The account continues on the next page.
Names hidden beneath the FBI b6/b7C redactions are not reconstructed. All third-party statements are attributed reports.
267:
BU 92-61 — E COVER PAGE.
Continuation: A source reported [REDACTED] instructions to handle certain matters but could give no further details.
On April 29, 1959, [REDACTED] advised that STEVE CANNAROZZO, FRED RANDACCIO, PATSY NATARELLI and other suspected numbers operators had frequented the Keith Theater at 261 Main Street, alleged by the source to be the current Buffalo numbers-racket headquarters.
Information received as early as October 1948 from the Buffalo Police Department described a loan-shark service reportedly operated by STEVE CANNAROZZO under the fictitious name Bison Supply Company, making short-term loans to gamblers, racketeers and bookmakers. A source claimed that an enforcement squad headed by CANNAROZZO would collect delinquent debts, and described the interest rates as exorbitant. These are historical allegations.
On February 5, 1959, Dun and Bradstreet records gave this background: STEVE CANNAROZZO's father, VICTOR CANNAROZZO, was born in Buffalo in 1902 and worked as steward of Buffalo Waiters Alliance Local 196 for 10 years before 1941. In 1941 VICTOR purchased an interest in Madison Cab Company. He was listed as president of Fadison [as printed] Cab Company and secretary of Auto Club Garage, which supplied gasoline and mechanical service to Madison Cab Company. The account continues.
All named assertions reflect the visible FBI document; redacted identities remain [REDACTED].
268:
BU 92-61 — F COVER PAGE.
According to a Dun and Bradstreet report, Madison Cab Company owned approximately 35 taxicabs and leased about 60 others.
PATSY NATARELLI, described as an associate of CANNAROZZO and RANDACCIO, was believed to be PASQUALE NATARELLI. The report supplied a background record:
Name: PASQUALE NATARELLI. Aliases: Patty, Patsy. Race: White. Sex: Male. Date of birth: July 9, 1910. Place of birth: Buffalo, New York. Age as recorded: 48. Residence: 60 Manchester Street, Buffalo, New York. Height: 5 feet 6 inches. Weight: 186 pounds. Build: Stocky. Hair: Brown. Eyes: Brown. Complexion: Fair. Marital status: Married. [REDACTED]. Characteristics: Very dapper and neat, well dressed. FBI No.: 317719. Attica Prison No.: 6478.
On June 22, 1956, the New York State Parole Office reportedly stated NATARELLI was regarded as the 'No. 1 man' among Buffalo criminal elements and claimed crimes by out-of-town hoodlums needed to be cleared through him. The same record says he was sentenced at Buffalo on March 16, 1934, for second-degree robbery, to 14 years, and released on parole November 22, 1942, with parole continued until February 16, 1949. Further background is continued on the next page.
Statements are attributed to the cited records; FBI withholding marks b6 and b7C preserved.
269:
BU 92-61 — G COVER PAGE.
Continuation of PASQUALE 'PATSY' NATARELLI's background: the report described him as a principal suspect in the gangland killing of LYMAN MILLER, who was shot on Buffalo streets in the early 1950s. This is a report of investigative suspicion, not a finding of guilt.
[REDACTED] advised that police records regarded NATARELLI as a well-known Buffalo hoodlum, formerly close to JOE DI CARLO, and that in 1956 he was considered an associate of FREDDY RANDACCIO.
According to New York State Parole Office information, in 1949 NATARELLI was a salesman for [REDACTED] American Flag Company, Chippewa Street, Buffalo. He was arrested January 30, 1951, in Rochester on a charge of common gambling involving lottery tickets, sentenced to three months at Monroe County Penitentiary, and fined $500.
A 1951 FBI interview concerning interstate transportation of lottery tickets recorded his claim that he owned a cleaning and tailoring business at 241 Vermont Avenue, Buffalo. Police searched his automobile and reportedly found approximately 1,300 Treasury Balance Lottery tickets, leading to his arrest.
On May 13, 1959, [REDACTED] stated that their department did not believe all Buffalo numbers operations were controlled by one group or syndicate. The account continues on the following page.
Redacted source identities are not reconstructed.
270:
BU 92-61 — H COVER PAGE.
Continuation of May 13, 1959 information: a source stated there was close cooperation among white gamblers and numerous Negro numbers banks operating in and around Buffalo. [REDACTED] believed an organized group was more likely to control bookmaking on horse races and sports than the numbers operation.
[REDACTED] said the department had been vigorously investigating Buffalo gambling, was aware of FREDDY RANDACCIO's alleged leadership role, and was considering full-time surveillance and periodic questioning of him and his associates to disrupt gambling activity. The source said this might cause him to abandon gambling-related activities.
On April 18, 1959, a source described as an ex-convict who had furnished reliable information to the Buffalo FBI office supplied an account of acquaintances in the Niagara Falls criminal element. Multiple identities and material facts are [REDACTED]. The visible text says several persons had reportedly gone missing from Niagara Falls in recent months, and the informant believed they might have been victims of foul play. The narrative continues on the next page.
The FBI document records the source's views; it does not establish that crimes occurred. All original b6/b7C/b7D redactions remain indicated as [REDACTED].
271:
BU 92-61 — I COVER PAGE (page 271 of scan).
Continuation of a redacted FBI informant account concerning disappearances in Niagara Falls, New York. A source said he was only casually acquainted with [REDACTED], could not supply a reason for the disappearances of the three people mentioned, and referred to the recent murder of ARTHUR DI LUCA of Niagara Falls.
The source further related a statement made on April 11, 1959 by a person [REDACTED], whom the source described as a stooge for STEVE MAGADDINO. The reported statement concerned contacting an individual in Niagara Falls, Ontario, Canada, for a purpose concealed by redaction. The discussion alleges movement of persons between Canada and Niagara Falls, New York, but nearly all names, circumstances, and purposes are concealed. The informant explicitly characterized part of his interpretation as conjecture.
Another confidential source described SAMUEL RANGATORE as an 'errand boy' for STEVE MAGADDINO in Niagara Falls and expressed an opinion about possible labor-union connections. The source identity and supporting particulars are [REDACTED].
The original document marks withheld material b6, b7C, and b7D. Allegations and speculation are attributed to informants; no conclusions about missing persons are independently established here.
272:
BU 92-61 — J COVER PAGE (page 272 of scan).
A confidential source continued to describe an unidentified individual as 'STEVE MAGADDINO's man' in Niagara Falls and mentioned the International Hod Carriers Union from New York City. The source said he knew MAGADDINO fairly well but was unable to provide specific information on the alleged activity.
Another source described STEVE MAGADDINO and his immediate relatives as a close-knit family who did not trust outsiders with knowledge of illegal activities. A source contacted again on May 13, 1959 was unable to supply further information.
SAM RANGATORE reportedly resided at 611 Hyde Park Boulevard, Niagara Falls, New York. Niagara Falls Police Department records, as reported by the FBI, reflected three illegal-parking violations in 1938 and described him as 48 years of age and a 'front man' for STEVE MAGADDINO. On May 13, 1959 a source reported personally observing RANGATORE regularly walking and conversing seriously with STEVE MAGADDINO during early morning hours in the parking area of Magaddino Memorial Chapel on Niagara Street, Niagara Falls.
Other names and locations are [REDACTED]. FBI assertions and source interpretations are not findings of guilt.
273:
BU 92-61 — K COVER PAGE (page 273 of scan).
Continuation of information about Magaddino Memorial Chapel on Niagara Street, Niagara Falls. A confidential source stated in December 1957 that a redacted individual had no criminal record at the Niagara Falls Police Department but was frequently seen with STEVE MAGADDINO or his brother ANTONIO MAGADDINO. The source said the person formerly operated as a gambler in Niagara Falls and that rumors persisted about Magaddino interests in those gambling establishments.
On April 15, 1959 a Buffalo FBI source reported seeing FRED RANDACCIO on two occasions during the first week of April at Andy's Cafe, 280 Terrace, with a younger man of Italian extraction. Details about the younger person, his employment and a prior arrest are [REDACTED].
On April 27, 1959 a source reported no additional information concerning the subject's current activities and said JAMES LA DUCA, the subject's son-in-law, was still absent from home; the source did not know La Duca's whereabouts.
On April 20, 1959 another source reported no new information about the subject, and said ANTONIO MAGADDINO was still absent from Niagara Falls. The narrative continues on the next scan.
Source identities and various details are [REDACTED] (b6/b7C/b7D).
274:
BU 92-61 — L COVER PAGE (page 274 of scan).
Continuation of a source's account that ANTONIO MAGADDINO's absence from Niagara Falls may have been intended to avoid service of a subpoena by the New York State Investigation Commission. The source could not establish Antonio's whereabouts.
On May 19, 1959 a Buffalo FBI source reported observing several automobiles arrive at STEVE MAGADDINO's summer home in the Town of Cambria at approximately 11:00 p.m. on May 16. The cars approached without headlights; a few lights were turned on after the occupants entered the house. The visitors stayed briefly and left. The source could not identify the occupants or provide further information. Except for this event and occasional family checks, the source had observed little activity there during the preceding six or seven months.
An April 13, 1959 report concerned an individual described as the head of a numbers racket in Lackawanna, New York, who was reportedly being investigated by the New York State Investigation Commission. The source could provide no information about any connection to STEVE MAGADDINO or VINCENT SCRO.
Names, portions of identities, and several clauses remain [REDACTED]. These are attributed informant observations and allegations.
275:
UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE — FEDERAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
FBI report dated May 26, 1959. Office: Buffalo, New York. Buffalo file 92-61; Bureau file 92-2924. Title: STEVE MAGADDINO. Character: ANTI-RACKETEERING.
SYNOPSIS: The two daughters and wife of the subject formed a new corporation in Niagara County, New York, in connection with a linen supply company operated by [REDACTED].
FBI warning: SUBJECT SHOULD BE CONSIDERED ARMED AND DANGEROUS DUE TO THE FACT THAT HE HAS A PERMIT TO CARRY A GUN.
DETAILS: A previous report discussed the interests of STEVE MAGADDINO and other family members, including [REDACTED] and VINCENT SCRO, in Camellia Linen Supply Company, 706 East Market Street, Niagara Falls. A May 1, 1959 Niagara Falls Gazette article, 'Firm Bought by Wives of 3 Probe Figures,' reported that Mrs. ARCANGELA P. SCRO, Mrs. ANGELINE MONTANA, and Mrs. CARMELA MAGADDINO (identified in the document as wives of Vincent Scro, [REDACTED], and Steve Magaddino, respectively), all of Dana Drive, Town of Lewiston, filed a deed with the County Clerk's Office in Lockport for a property at 1114 Haeberle [line continues on next page].
Visible text preserved as a draft; concealed passages are [REDACTED].
276:
BU 92-61 — continuation (original PDF page 276; printed report page -2*-).
Avenue in Niagara Falls. This article pointed out that the tax stamps on the deed to the property at this address indicate the purchase price of this property by the above three mentioned individuals at about $9,000.00.

This article further pointed out that on April 27, 1959, the above three women filed a Certificate of Incorporation at the County Clerk's Office in Lockport, New York, to form a new corporation. The Certificate noted that 'this corporation is organized to acquire the property, rights, privileges, and franchises, good will, and name of an existing domestic corporation.'

Mrs. STEVE MAGADDINO is a partner in the Camellia Linen Supply Company and as of May 11, 1959, the Camellia Linen Supply Company formerly located on Market Street was moved to the newly acquired property at 1114 Haeberle Avenue, Niagara Falls.

The newspaper article mentioned above further points out that listed as new directors for the newly formed corporation, the name of which was not given in the newspaper article, were EMORY R. DAVIS, Jamestown, New York; WILLIAM J. LOESER, Hamburg, New York; and FRANK H. STEVENSON, Buffalo, New York. This article further pointed out that in addition, Mr. DAVIS was listed as President, and Mr. STEVENSON as Secretary, and according to the filing of the Certificate, each director holds 300 shares of the 1500 shares of capital stock in the company but all shares have no par value.

SUBJECT SHOULD BE CONSIDERED ARMED AND DANGEROUS DUE TO THE FACT THAT HE HAS A PERMIT TO CARRY A GUN.
